Short broad-bladed swords, yew bows, shields, knives (in Isengard)}} {{Quote|‘There are Orcs, very many of them,’ he said. ‘And some are large and evil: black Uruks of Mordor. For the moment they are hanging back, but there is something else there. A great cave-troll, I think, or more than one. There is no hope of escape that way.’|[[Gandalf]] in [[The Bridge of Khazad-dûm|Chapter 5]] of {{LotRlink|media=book1}}}} '''Uruk-hai''' (a pure [[Black Speech]] form, rendered as '''Uruks''' in English) were brutal warriors of [[Middle-earth]], and the strongest breed of [[Orcs|Orc]]. The term ''Uruk-hai'' refers to those bred in [[Isengard]] as [[Isengarders]] as well the enhanced breed amid [[Sauron]]'s forces in [[Mordor]]. == History == Described as elite "black Orcs", these were the first Orc-kind in [[Middle-earth]] to be referred to as ''uruks'', originating centuries before the Great Years when they first appeared out of Mordor in the year [[TA 2475|2475]] of the [[Third Age]], making assaults in [[Ithilien]] and destroyed the [[Cities|city]] of [[Osgiliath]].{{LotRlink}}, [[Appendix A]], iv. "Gondor and the heirs of Anárion", pg. 1053 (50th Anniversary One-Volume Edition) The Uruks in the service of [[Barad-dûr]] used the symbol of the red [[Eye of Sauron]], which was also painted on their [[shield]]s. In [[TA 2480]], Sauron also populated the [[Misty Mountains]] with his creatures of evil, including Uruks of Mordor. [[File:Uruk-hai N Chacin.png|thumb|280px|left|An Uruk of Isengard, depicted by [[:Category:Art by Nicolas Chacin|Nicolas Chacin]]]] Uruk-hai were later bred almost a millennium later by the [[Order of Wizards|wizard]] [[Saruman|Saruman the White]] late in the [[Third Age]] by his dark arts at Isengard. They were "large, swart" and "slant-eyed".{{LotRlink}}, {{LotRlink|media=book2}}, Book Three, Ch. III: "[[The Uruk-hai]]", pg. 451 (50th Anniversary One-Volume Edition) In the late Third Age, [[Boromir]] spotted Uruks of [[Mordor]] in [[Khazad-dûm|Moria]] moments before the skirmish in the [[Chamber of Mazarbul]] between the [[Fellowship of the Ring (group)|Fellowship of the Ring]] and the many Orc-kinds inhabiting Moria.{{LotRlink}}, {{LotRlink|media=book1}}, Book Two, Ch. V: "[[The Bridge of Khazad-dûm]]", pg. 338 In the [[War of the Ring]], the Uruk-hai made up a large part of [[Saruman's army]], together with the [[Dunlendings]], [[Men|man]]-enemies of [[Rohan]]. Saruman originally commanded some Uruks which had come down from the Misty Mountains to serve the Wizard as mercenaries.{{LotRlink}}, ''[[The Return of the King]]'': [[Appendix A]] He also later bred his own Uruks, and this was kept secret from [[White Council|The White Council]] at the time.[[Unfinished Tales of Númenor and Middle-earth|The Unfinished Tales of Middle-earth and Numenor]]: Notes 7. The Uruk-hai were speculated by [[Treebeard]] to have either been Men who Saruman "ruined" or were created as hybrids of orcs and men, due to their larger size and resistance to sunlight. Treebeard called this possible crossbreeding "A black evil"{{LotRlink}}, {{LotRlink|media=book2}}, Book Three, Ch. IV: "[[Treebeard (chapter)|Treebeard]]". There were also other creatures in Saruman's armies, and under his command in the Shire, that appear to have been hybrids. These "[[half-orcs]]" were as tall as Men, sallow-skinned and are never described simply as Orcs, in contrast to the Uruk-hai. [[File:TtT - Uglúk daytime.jpeg|left|thumb|Uglúk, an Uruk of Isengard as portrayed in films]] Uruks of Isengard used an "S" [[Angerthas|Elf-rune]] wrought in white metal on the front of their iron helms. It was clear this stood for Saruman, because their shields had a small White Hand centered on a black field.{{LotRlink}}, {{LotRlink|media=book2}}, Book Three, Ch. I: "[[The Departure of Boromir]]" [[Aragorn II|Aragorn]] commented, when first encountering them, that their gear was not in the manner of other Orcs at all. Instead of the curved [[scimitar]], they used short, broad-bladed swords. Their great [[bow|bows]] were made of yew wood, of the same length and shape as those of Men.{{LotRlink}}, {{LotRlink|media=book2}}, Book Three, Ch. I: "[[The Departure of Boromir]]" Saruman's army of Uruk-hai fought against [[King of Rohan|King]] [[Théoden]] of Rohan and his people in the [[Second Battle of the Fords of Isen]] and the [[Battle of the Hornburg]] together with [[Northern Orcs]], [[Dunlendings|Dunlandish Men]] and [[half-orcs]].{{LotRlink}}, {{LotRlink|media=book2}}, Book Three, Ch. VII: "[[Helm's Deep (chapter)|Helm's Deep]]" [[File:Uruk-hai upclose.jpg|thumb|360px|Uruk warriors portrayed in film|alt=]] Saruman appeared to aid his Orcs with wizardry as well: when Aragorn, [[Gimli]], and [[Legolas]] followed the party of Uruks who had kidnapped [[Meriadoc Brandybuck|Merry]] and [[Peregrin Took|Pippin]], Saruman's will caused weariness of the heart for the pursuers and lent speed to the Orcs.{{LotRlink}}, {{LotRlink|media=book2}}, Book Three, Ch. III: "[[The Uruk-hai]]" This was [[Saruman's scouts|the group]] that had slain [[Boromir]], and was later annihilated by [[Éomer]] and his [[éored]].{{LotRlink}}, {{LotRlink|media=book2}}, Book Three, Ch. II: "[[The Riders of Rohan (chapter)|The Riders of Rohan]]" [[File:Shagrat.jpg|thumb|210px|Shagrat of Cirith Ungol]] Within Mordor, some Uruk-hai were stationed at the [[Tower of Cirith Ungol]]. After escaping from there, the [[Hobbits]] [[Frodo Baggins|Frodo]] and [[Samwise Gamgee|Sam]] saw Uruks march from [[Durthang]] towards the [[Black Gate]] amidst the mass-movement of all of Sauron's remaining forces.{{LotRlink}}, Vol. III: {{LotRlink|media=book3}}, Book Six, Chapter II: "[[The Land of Shadow]]" The Uruks of [[Minas Morgul]] answered to the [[Witch-king of Angmar|Witch-king]], who led the attack upon [[Gondor]]. But at the [[Tower of Cirith Ungol]] many of them were [[Quarrel|killed]] by their own [[Mordor-orcs|Mordor-orc]] brethren over [[Frodo Baggins|Frodo]]'s [[Mithril Coat]], including [[Gorbag]], one of their leaders. Eventually, [[Shagrat]] brought the coat to the [[Mouth of Sauron]] and told the authorities of [[Barad-dûr]] that some rebel Uruk-hai were on the loose since some escaped the tower. == Etymology == In [[Black Speech]] of Mordor, ''Uruk-hai'' was a collective term that meant "Orc-folk".[[Parma Eldalamberon]], no. XVII, entry ''Urukhai'' on p. 136 The name "Uruk-hai" has the element ''Uruk'', a Black Speech word related to "orc" and to the (Valinórean) Quenya word ''urko'' (Ñoldorin Quenya: ''orko'') of the same meaning. The element hai means "folk," so "Uruk-hai" is "Orc-folk." A similar term is [[Olog-hai]] ("troll-folk"), used for a breed of especially strong and vicious trolls capable of surviving sunlight. [[Christopher Tolkien]] describes "uruks" as an anglicization of "Uruk-hai," and his father used the two terms interchangeably a number of times. == In adaptations == [[File:Ralph Bakshi's Uruk-Hai.PNG|thumb|240px|Saruman's Orcs, possibly Uruks (1978)]] === ''The Lord of the Rings'' (1978 animated film) === While their role in the books is recreated for this film, the word "Uruk" is never used in {{LotRlink|media=film}} nor are they clearly distinguished from other Orcs. Hence, it is unknown if they exist in this adaptation. === ''The Lord of the Rings'' film trilogy === {{Quote|Do you know how the Orcs first came to being? They were Elves once, taken by the [[dark powers]], tortured and mutilated. A ruined and terrible form of life. And now, perfected. My fighting Uruk-hai.|Saruman}} All Uruks depicted in {{LotRlink|media=films}} by [[Peter Jackson]] are recognizable by their broader stature and long hair resembling that of the [[Isengard]] Uruk-hai. [[Gorbag]] was therefore depicted as a black Uruk, being instead skinny, with the natural slouch of other common Orcs. [[File:Isengard_soldiers.jpg|400px|thumb|The Uruk-hai force assembled at the foot of the [[Orthanc]]|left]] In trilogy, [[Saruman]] appeared to believe that the Uruks were his invention. In {{LotRlink|media=film1|''The Fellowship of the Ring''}}, [[Gandalf]] mentions Saruman creating Uruks by crossbreeding "Orcs with goblin men." He states that they are "An army that can move in sunlight and cover great distance at speed." However, the film-lore book {{LotRlink|media=ww}} clears up this discrepancy by explaining that Saruman was in fact only replicating Sauron's method. Sauron's Uruks, seen in {{LotRlink|media=film3}}, have noticeably rougher features than Saruman's. Saruman's Uruk-hai are shown as being released from a kind of membrane in the mud deep under Isengard (special commentary on the DVD edition explained that they were trying to base the scene on an early description of Tolkien's that Orcs "worm their way out of the ground like maggots"). The Uruks of Mordor are frequently seen: the invented character [[Murgash]] is one of them, at the [[Siege of Gondor]], and many others march through the Orc-camp encountered by Sam and Frodo in western Mordor. Most notably, [[Shagrat]], in the [[Tower of Cirith Ungol]], is portrayed as an Uruk.[[File:Uruk-hai in rain.jpg|alt=|thumb|240px|Uruk-hai in full armour in Peter Jackson's {{LotRlink|media=film2}}]] ==== Weaponry & army composition ==== His Uruks army includes pikemen, swordsmen, crossbowmen, sappers, [[Saruman's scouts|scouts]], and [[berserkers]]. The berserkers are even larger and more vicious Uruks. They shave their heads and fill their helmets with human blood, so that when they put on the helmets the blood runs down their backs and its scent sends them into a killing frenzy. They carry double-bent swords. These swords were feared by their [[Rohirrim]] enemies for good reason. First, they had double spikes on the end (used for hamstringing or disemboweling horses). Second, the tremendous strength of the berserkers could easily take the head off of any human. Last, they had a keen cutting edge that could easily cut through the leather armor of the Rohirrim (for the massive swords were powerful enough to cut through even steel armor). The sappers were responsible for crewing the ballistae, handling the ladders and carrying Saruman's bombs. The army additionally had many hundreds of pikemen and a smaller count of deadly crossbowmen. Normal Uruk infantry wielded swords and shields. These swords would maximize the brute strength of the Uruks, being able to cut off limbs and heads very easily. They also sometimes use bladed shields with the White Hand painted on them, as seen on [[Amon Hen]] during [[Aragorn II|Aragorn]]'s fight against [[Lurtz]]. These were broad shields, made of durable iron that could defend well against incoming attacks and would provide an alternative weapon by using the bladed side, should the Uruk lose his other weapon. Scouts wear light, leather armor and have leather helmets with no crests or brims, and wield short swords, axes, daggers, and powerful bows of yew with a tremendous draw weight. Their armor is grey and is made up of large lames and has a groin guard. Underneath is a layer of chainmail that covers the torso, half the arm and a small fraction of the legs. They also wear arm armor but they have bare legs. For footwear they have puttees and sandals that are covered by foot and leg armor.[[File:Uruk-hai Berserker TTT.jpg|alt=|left|thumb|260px|An Uruk "Berserker"]]As the Isengard Uruk-hai were an army that was being rapidly grown, mass production of arms was required to equip them quickly. The metal weapons used by the Isengard uruks, as depicted in ''The Fellowship of the Ring'', are made from iron melted in a foundry, cast in open molds, then [[Wikipedia:Forge|forged]], and finally finished by sharpening on grindstones. Armor and helmets are also seen being hammered and shaped en masse. Though the weapons and armor were competently crafted, the quality is depicted as relatively crude compared to the more finely honed weapons of the Elves, Men, and [[Dwarves]]. This lack of quality is not shown as hindering effectiveness. === Ambiguity in films and games === In some adaptations, the label of "Black Uruk" is made synonymous with ''Black Orc'' (such as in [[Electronic Arts|EA]]'s {{LotRlink|media=battle2rise|''The Rise of the Witch-king''}}) or even ''[[Mordor-orcs|Morannon Orc]]'' - on the grounds that all three names denote a tougher breed of Mordor-indigenous Orc. ==== ''Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor'' and ''Shadow of War'' ==== Uruk-hai, or "Uruks" as they are termed in the games, appear in both {{Melink|media=mordor}} and its sequel {{Melink|media=war|''Shadow of War''}} as the games' primary antagonists throughout the land of Mordor. A wide variety of Uruks are depicted, including a hierarchy of captains and warchiefs within Sauron's army. Some are also shown to be necromancers, wielding dark sorcery. Their appearances in these games do not resemble their film depiction.[[File:Lurtz birth.jpg|alt=|thumb|230x230px|Lurtz observing his strength after being born from the mud of Isengard]] == Notable Uruk-hai == *[[Uglúk]] was one of Saruman's Uruk-hai who commanded the scouts that attacked the Fellowship of the Ring and captured Merry and Pippin. Uglúk later died fighting Éomer when his band was slain by Rohirrim. *[[Mauhúr]] led an attack on the [[Rohirrim]] surrounding Uglúk's company, but failed to drive them off. *[[Lugdush]] was one of Saruman's Uruks, likely a trusted subordinate of Uglúk. He was tasked with guarding the captive Merry and Pippin. He was presumably killed with other Orcs by the Riders of Rohan near [[Fangorn Forest]]. === In adaptations === *[[Lurtz]] was a character created specifically for Peter Jackson's movie {{LotRlink|media=film1}}. He is the first Uruk-hai bred in Isengard, and kills the first thing he sees, strangling the Orc who oversaw his birth. As the first Uruk made, he is shown to be the strongest Uruk, and his skin appears a muddy brown instead of the other Uruk-hai's more reddish skin. Saruman places him in command of the "Uruk-hai scouts" and sends him along with a company of Uruks to find the Fellowship of the Ring. He kills Boromir with a bow, shooting him three times, and then violently duels with Aragorn, in which he loses his arm, is impaled by Aragorn's sword, and finally beheaded. He was portrayed by [[New Zealand]] actor [[Lawrence Makoare]]. == See also == *[[Olog-hai]] == Translations == {| class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Show" data-collapsetext="Hide" style="border: 1px solid #a6a6a6; width:65%;" | width="300" |'''Foreign Language''' | width="300" |'''Translated name''' |- |Amharic |ዑሩክ፡ሃኢ |- |Arabic |أوروك-هاي |- |Armenian |ՈՒրուկ-հաի |- |Belarusian Cyrillic |Урук-хаі |- |Bengali |উড়ুক-হয় |- |Bosnian |Juruk-hai |- |Bulgarian Cyrillic |Урук-хай |- |Chinese |乌鲁克族 |- |Czech |Skurut-hai |- |Esperanto |Uruk-hajoj |- |Georgian |ურუქ-ჰაი |- | Greek |Ουρούκ-Χάι |- |Gujarati |ઉરુક-હૈ |- |Hebrew |אורוק האי |- |Hindi |उरुक हाइ |- |Japanese |ウルク＝ハイ |- |Kannada |ಉರುಕ್-ಹೈ |- | Kazakh |Ұрұк-һаі (Cyrillic) Uruk-hai (Latin) |- |Korean | 우르크하이 |- |Kyrgyz Cyrillic |Урук-Гаи |- |Macedonian Cyrillic |Урук-хаи |- |Marathi |ऊरुखै |- |Mongolian Cyrillic |Урук-hаи |- |Nepalese |उरुक हाइ |- |Persian |اوروک-هی |- |Punjabi |ਊਰੁਖੈ |- |Russian |Урук-Хай |- |Serbian |Урук-хаи (Cyrillic) Uruk-hai (Latin) |- |Sinhalese |ඌරුක්-හ්ඓ |- |Tajik Cyrillic |Урук-ха |- |Tamil |உருக்-ஹை |- |Telugu |ఉరుక్-హై |- | Thai |อูรุก-ไฮ |- |Ukrainian Cyrillic |Урук-хай |- |Uzbek |Урук-ҳаи (Cyrillic) Uruk-hai (Latin) |- |Yiddish |ורוק-האַי |} {{Clear}} == References == {{scroll box| }} == External links == *[[Wikipedia:List of weapons and armour in Middle-earth|List of weapons and armour in Middle-earth]] at Wikipedia {{Races}} [[Category:Orc-kind]] [[Category:Uruk-hai]] [[Category:Characters in Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor]] [[Category:Characters in Middle-earth: Shadow of War]] [[Category:Black Speech names & words]] [[de:Uruk-hai]] [[es:Uruk-hai]] [[fi:Uruk-Hai]] [[fr:Uruk-hai]] [[he:אורוק האי]] [[it:Uruk-hai]] [[nl:Uruk-hai]] [[pl:Uruk-hai]] [[pt-br:Uruk]] [[ru:Урук-хай]] [[sk:Uruk-hai]]
